high_risk_moment: Vendor recommendation is generated before an employer reviews the application
stakeholder: Older, Black, or disabled applicant evaluated through enabled vendor screening features
harm_description: An opaque vendor recommendation or customer configuration may score, rank, withhold, or deprioritize applicants at scale while employer and vendor accountability remains unclear.
existing_controls: Historical evidence: the cited public record establishes the dispute and procedural posture, not the existence or effectiveness of Workday or customer bias safeguards. Current FairScreen control: offline shadow isolation retains the complete queue and denies status-write access, but vendor access, version, and validation evidence remain open in GAP-04 and GAP-05.
proposed_controls: Close GAP-04 and GAP-05: contract for evaluation-data and log access; inventory every enabled feature and customer rule; pin approved model and configuration versions; test end-to-end applicant visibility and subgroup first-review-band exposure; prohibit silent vendor changes and application withholding.
human_oversight: The employer recruiter must see every complete application and original evidence, review every application within the SLA before closing a requisition, record each human status change, and add a job-related reason and appeal notice for an adverse status; an independent reviewer audits samples and appeals without vendor or hiring-manager conflict.
owner: Vendor Risk and Talent Operations Lead
monitoring_metric: Complete-application visibility and review-SLA rate; confidence bounds for subgroup first-review-band exposure and qualified-applicant recall gap; undocumented model or configuration changes; appeal overturn rate
trigger_threshold: One hidden or overdue complete application; one unregistered vendor or configuration change; lower 95 percent confidence bound for a cohort assignment-rate ratio below 0.80; upper bound for absolute recall gap above 5 percentage points; or an underpowered or inconclusive cohort at the release gate
response_action: Disable the vendor recommendation integration, restore chronological manual review, preserve end-to-end logs, notify the vendor and review panel, re-review affected applications, and require independent validation before re-enable.

high_risk_moment: Candidate completes an automated parser or assessment and needs an accessible alternative
stakeholder: Applicant with a disability or assistive-technology need
harm_description: An inaccessible assessment, absent notice, or slow accommodation path can measure disability-related interaction rather than job ability and silently screen out a qualified applicant.
existing_controls: Historical evidence: EEOC guidance describes the general risk and the litigation alleges disability discrimination, without establishing each customer control. Current FairScreen control: no live candidate is exposed in offline shadow mode; notice and accommodation journeys are designed but GAP-03 testing remains open.
proposed_controls: Close GAP-03: give advance plain-language notice, a WCAG 2.2 AA candidate journey, an accessible accommodation request, compatible formats, a no-penalty manual alternative, deadline extension, and separation of disability information from model inputs and recruiter scoring.
human_oversight: An accessibility coordinator acknowledges a request within one business day, freezes automated scoring, provides an equivalent alternative before the deadline, and documents the resolution; an independent appeal reviewer can reinstate the candidate and pause the assessment.
monitoring_metric: Notice delivery rate; WCAG A/AA defect count; accommodation response time; completion and advance-rate gap for accommodated applicants
trigger_threshold: Any missing notice, any open severity-1 or severity-2 accessibility defect, any request unresolved after two business days, or an unexplained completion or advance-rate gap
response_action: Pause the affected assessment, extend the candidate deadline, provide manual evaluation with no penalty, re-review all similarly affected applications, log the incident, and require independent accessibility evidence before restart.

high_risk_moment: Application and voluntary audit attributes move across the candidate portal, ATS, model host, and segregated audit environment
stakeholder: Applicant whose identity, employment history, or voluntary demographic attribute is processed
harm_description: Unauthorized access, purpose expansion, insecure transfer, excessive retention, or accidental joining of audit attributes to hiring data can expose sensitive information, enable discrimination, or deny effective data rights across vendor boundaries.
existing_controls: Current FairScreen control: shadow evaluation admits synthetic data by default and no live or identifiable applicant data; real-person-derived de-identified history requires prior provenance, transformation, linkage-risk, retention, and access approval. The broader GAP-04 rights, transfer, deletion, and vendor evidence remains open.
proposed_controls: Close GAP-04: enforce field allowlists and purpose binding; isolate and restrict audit attributes; encrypt and log access and transfer; approve de-identification, retention, and rights workflows; contract vendor and subprocessor duties; test deletion, access, linkage, re-identification, and incident paths before real-person-derived data use.
human_oversight: The Data Protection Officer approves each purpose, dataset, transformation, vendor, transfer, retention period, and access role; privacy and security reviewers can stop ingestion, revoke access, order deletion, investigate an incident, and keep live use blocked until evidence is independently accepted.
monitoring_metric: Unauthorized-access count; audit attributes reaching model or hiring users; successful linkage or re-identification count; unapproved transfer or vendor change count; rights-request and deletion deadline compliance
trigger_threshold: Any unauthorized access, one audit attribute reaching the model or hiring user, one successful re-identification in the registered test, one unapproved transfer or subprocessor, or inability to locate or delete an in-scope record
response_action: Stop ingestion and recommendations, isolate affected stores and credentials, preserve logs, notify the Data Protection Officer and Legal, identify affected records and people, execute the approved incident and rights process, require vendor remediation, and obtain independent restart approval.

high_risk_moment: Eligibility gate before any recruiter sees the application
stakeholder: Older applicant subject to a sex-specific age threshold
harm_description: An impermissible configured rule can invisibly end access to employment before qualifications receive human consideration, with time-sensitive income and dignity effects.
existing_controls: Historical response: at settlement, iTutorGroup had ceased U.S. tutor hiring; the decree imposed prospective training, policy, injunction, notification, interview, and monitoring duties if hiring resumed. Current FairScreen control: offline shadow isolation and a drafted job-criteria registry exist, but GAP-01 and GAP-02 tests remain open.
proposed_controls: Close GAP-01 and GAP-02: maintain an approved job-criteria registry; prohibit protected traits and unapproved proxies; make status-write access unavailable to the model; regression-test every rule; keep every application visible; require human review for every status change and provide a reason and appeal for adverse status.
human_oversight: Before any human non-advance, an authorized recruiter sees the original application, approved criterion, supporting evidence, uncertainty, and protected fields hidden; the recruiter has time and authority to advance, and a separate appeal reviewer can reinstate within two business days.
monitoring_metric: Automatic status-change count; complete-application visibility and review-SLA rate; active criteria referencing protected traits or unapproved proxies; appeal overturn rate
trigger_threshold: Any model-written status change, prohibited criterion, hidden or overdue complete application, missing human review record, or adverse status missing reason, notice, or appeal
response_action: Immediately pause recommendations, restore the chronological manual queue, preserve model and review logs, notify Legal and the Chief People Officer, identify every affected application, and complete human re-review before restart.

high_risk_moment: Model-generated review order before the first interview shortlist
stakeholder: Women and non-traditional applicants whose resume language differs from historical selections
harm_description: Historical selection patterns and gender-correlated proxies can lower otherwise qualified applicants in the queue, reducing recruiter attention without an explicit protected-trait input.
existing_controls: Historical response: Amazon reportedly tested and edited the prototype and ultimately abandoned it, without a published deployed remediation audit. Current FairScreen control: the complete queue remains available and shadow outputs cannot affect applicants, but GAP-02 has no passing two-run evidence.
proposed_controls: Close GAP-02: pre-register deterministic band, precision, cohort, confidence-bound, and alternative-selection rules; require independent job-related labels, non-overlapping evaluation sets, proxy analysis, intersectional exposure and qualified-applicant recall tests, and independent validation; never hide or truncate the queue.
human_oversight: A recruiter reviews original job evidence rather than a single score, can advance any applicant, must review every complete application before closing the requisition, and can pause the tool; a separate appeal reviewer can reverse a human decision.
monitoring_metric: Confidence bounds for subgroup first-review-band assignment-rate ratio and qualified-applicant recall gap; overall qualified recall; queue review-SLA rate; unresolved proxy count
trigger_threshold: Lower 95 percent confidence bound for any cohort assignment-rate ratio below 0.80; upper bound for absolute recall gap above 5 percentage points; overall recall below 95 percent; an underpowered or inconclusive cohort; one overdue application; or an unresolved proxy finding in either run
response_action: Block promotion or pause the affected requisition, switch to the manual rubric, investigate labels and features, test less-disparate valid alternatives under the adoption rule, and require an independent two-run re-validation before restart.
